habitat: Parties of six or more in dense riverside and hillside thickets, and in dense undergrowth in forest and bushveld. They scratch in debris and seldom rise above the lower stratum.
summary: A common resident. A very drab brown bird, dark brown above, with a white throat that contrasts with the dusky breast and flanks. The underparts are barely paler than the upper parts. The eyes are reddish. At close range a yellowish gape is discernible. The immature has redder edges to the wing feathers. Parties keep contact with a quiet chuckle or murmur. The Kemp paper name Terrestrial Bulbul and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Sombre Greenbul is olive, with a creamy-white eye. Terrestrial Brownbul is drab brown, with a white throat and reddish eyes.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. Dusky is not stored as a colour. The immature wing edges are only described as redder. The grade A call is from Grahamstown. No flight photograph was found. Population figures and the Kemp name Terrestrial Bulbul were left unchanged.
